messages.author: 2fdab239c1396fa6
messages.subject: Models hang on 'running chain 1...'
parts:
Dear developers,

In general, what things happen after calling runMCMC(), while the output is 'running chain 1...' but before the progress bar shows? For some of my models it seems to pause on that line for a considerable amount of time, sometimes more than an hour while it only a few minutes for the progress bar to complete afterwards. If you could give me an indication then it might help me to find any problems with the models. 

Thank you very much,

Oliver Stoner

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Models hang on 'running chain 1...'
parts:
Oliver, I'm surprised to hear that it can hang for that long.  There are a number of small things that happen inside runMCMC(), after the message "running chain 1" and before the MCMC begins sampling (and hence the progress bar appears).  The only one of those which I think could take significant time is a call to model$calculate(), which calculates all the log-densities for every node in the model (top-level parameters, latent states, and also the data likelihood), which is somewhat precautionary, but sometimes necessary to ensure the model is fully initialized before the MCMC actually begins.  If your model is large, this call to model$calculate() can take a while, but in that case the MCMC would also generally take a lot of time.  So I'm a little surprised.  If you're interested to share your model code, I can take a closer look.

Cheers,
Daniel

Here's code which should reproduce the problem I'm having. It's a hidden Markov model where the data is a matrix of values. In the matrix, the rows represent discrete time steps, where all columns in each row come from a rounded zero-inflated log-normal distribution, the parameters of which depend on an unobserved hidden Markov parameter which is shared by all columns.

 For me, it takes about an hour run do 2000 iterations on 2 chains, with most of the time taken up before the progress bar shows. Thanks again for your help.

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Models hang on 'running chain 1...'
parts:
Olivier, thanks for bringing this to my attention.  This is a bit of an over-sight on my part.

There were some recent changes in NIMBLE's MCMC system, w.r.t. how it handles thinning vs. burnin.  (Specifically, which happens first?  Are burnin samples discarded from *post-thinning* samples, or are burnin samples discarded first, and the remaining samples thinned?  To completely resolve this question, any entry point to NIMBLE's MCMC now discards burnin samples *first*, then the remaining samples are thinned, e.g. (10000 - 2000) / 10 = 800 posterior samples returned; see help(runMCMC), Details section).

A result of this change, as an implementation detail, is that burnin samples specified through runMCMC() do *not* trigger the MCMC progress bar to begin, and instead the progress bar begins once the *post burnin* samples are being collected (and simultaneously thinned).

That is what you're experiencing, the fact that the 1000 burnin samples do not trigger the progress bar, which only begins starting at sample # 1001.  In combination with the pre-processing that takes place (e.g., model$calculate(), and a few other things), it gives the behaviour you're seeing, which I successfully recreated.

The upshot is that everything is working correctly, only the progress bar is misleading.

Let me give a think about the best way to restructure the implementation to address this, which I agree is unsatisfying.

I'll be in touch.

Daniel

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Models hang on 'running chain 1...'
parts:
Oliver, I've taken a stab at this, and pushed the notion of burnin down to the lower-level mcmc$run method, rather than as a post-processing step within runMCMC where it happened previously.

These changes are available on the development branch of nimble.  If you're interested, you can install this developmental version using:

library(devtools)
install_github('nimble-dev/nimble', ref = 'devel', subdir = 'packages/nimble')
library(nimble)

Otherwise, these changes will be available in our next minor release of the package, which I think will be coming in the next couple weeks.

Cheers,
Daniel
